name: Skydance Corporation

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (Skydance Corporation Dark Logo 2026.svg, the en.wikipedia.org Skydance infobox logo, 'used since 2026')

description: Skydance Corporation owns CBS and a library of cable channels (Nickelodeon, MTV, Comedy Central, BET), the Paramount+ and Pluto TV streaming services, and the Paramount Pictures and Skydance film and TV studios. It earns money from advertising on its TV networks and streaming, fees that cable and satellite distributors pay to carry its channels, Paramount+ subscriptions, and licensing its shows and films. On 2026-10-06 it completed a $31-per-share cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery (the HBO Max streaming service, the Warner Bros. studios and a large set of cable networks), funded by $41.4 billion of new senior secured bonds plus about $47 billion of new Class B stock sold to investors tied to the Ellison family and RedBird. All reported figures in this profile are Paramount Skydance's own through 2026-06-30; Warner Bros. Discovery was not yet consolidated.

corporateActions.text: Formerly Paramount Skydance (PSKY). Renamed Skydance on Oct 6, 2026, moving from Nasdaq to the NYSE as SKYD. The same day it completed its purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) for $31.02 a share in cash, about $78 billion in all.

sources.covers: name change from Paramount Skydance Corporation, Class B listing moved from Nasdaq to the NYSE, ticker PSKY changed to SKYD; CIK 0002041610 unchanged
completion of the Warner Bros. Discovery purchase at $31.01666668 per share in cash
merger consideration $31.00 plus $0.00277778 a day after 2026-09-30, $31.01666668 per share; aggregate consideration approximately $78 billion

gics.note: From the table in Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (raw wikitext read 2026-10-27): SKYD, 'Skydance', Communication Services, Movies & Entertainment, New York City, date shown 1994-09-30, CIK 0002041610. The table gives only sector and sub-industry, so industry group and industry are left null.

employees.note: About 17,600 full- and part-time employees in 30 countries plus about 3,600 project-based staff on the payroll (FY2025 10-K). This is before Warner Bros. Discovery joined on 2026-10-06; WBD's headcount was not read.

businessLines.name: TV Media
businessLines.how: Advertisers pay to air commercials on CBS and the cable networks; cable, satellite and streaming distributors pay monthly per-subscriber fees for the channels (affiliate fees) and the stations (retransmission fees); local stations pay for CBS network affiliation; syndicated shows are licensed to stations.
businessLines.description: CBS Television Network, CBS Stations (29 owned stations), international free-to-air networks (Network 10 in Australia, Channel 5 in the U.K.), domestic basic cable networks (MTV, Comedy Central, Paramount Network, Nickelodeon, BET Media Group, CBS Sports Network, Smithsonian Channel) and CBS Media Ventures (first-run syndication).

revenue.note: H1 2026: advertising $3,341M, affiliate and subscription $3,201M, licensing and other $252M. Predecessor H1 2025 $8,549M was on a different basis (included studios and Paramount+ with Showtime). FY2025 old-basis TV Media: $17,059M (Successor $7,082M + Predecessor $9,977M, simple sum of the two periods).

businessLines.revenueNote: H1 2026: advertising $3,341M, affiliate and subscription $3,201M, licensing and other $252M. operatingProfit.note: Margin 31.2% (derived: 2,118 / 6,794). Share of the three segments' Adjusted EBITDA of $2,935M: 72.2% (derived).

businessLines.name: Direct-to-Consumer
businessLines.how: Monthly subscriptions (directly and through third-party distributors such as app stores and cable bundles) for Paramount+, plus advertising on Paramount+ ad tiers and on free Pluto TV channels.
businessLines.description: Paramount+ (including Paramount+ with Showtime, and BET+ folded in during Q2 2026) and the free ad-supported Pluto TV.

revenue.note: H1 2026: advertising $1,052M, affiliate and subscription $3,820M. Predecessor H1 2025 $4,204M excluded Paramount+ with Showtime. FY2025 old-basis: $8,584M (Successor $3,497M + Predecessor $5,087M, simple sum).

businessLines.revenueNote: H1 2026: advertising $1,052M, affiliate and subscription $3,820M. Predecessor H1 2025 $4,204M excluded Paramount+ with Showtime. FY2025 old-basis: $8,584M (Successor $3,497M + Predecessor $5,087M, simple sum).

operatingProfit.note: Margin 12.7% (derived: 617 / 4,872). Share of the three segments' Adjusted EBITDA: 21.0% (derived). Predecessor H1 2025 Adjusted OIBDA was $48M on the old basis.

businessLines.name: Studios
businessLines.how: Ticket sales shared with theaters for films, and licensing fees from streaming services, TV networks and other platforms for films and series (a large part is licensed to Paramount's own platforms, with costs allocated by distribution window and no intersegment profit booked); film costs are expensed as content cost and marketing.
businessLines.description: CBS Studios, Paramount Television Studios, Nickelodeon Animation, Paramount Pictures, Paramount Animation, Miramax (rights joint venture with beIN Media Group), plus Skydance Animation, Film and Television, Paramount Sports Entertainment and Paramount Games Studio.

revenue.note: H1 2026: theatrical $290M, licensing and other $2,299M, advertising $8M. Predecessor H1 2025 Filmed Entertainment $1,317M was on the old, narrower basis (no TV studios). FY2025 old-basis Filmed Entertainment: $3,329M (Successor $1,736M + Predecessor $1,593M).

operatingProfit.note: Margin 7.7% (derived: 200 / 2,597). Share of the three segments' Adjusted EBITDA: 6.8% (derived). Q2 2026 alone: $36M on $1,314M.
